outcome: No event dated inside the window (26 Jan 2024 to 13 Oct 2026) that I could find settles or moves the general question of which finite sets C admit a countable universal C-free graph under strong (induced) embeddings; the general problem appears still open, but this is absence of evidence across searches, not a verified status. The two in-window items found concern different classes (rayless graphs with universal families, Dec 2025; minor-closed classes, Apr 2025). The pre-window literature decides many single-C and cycle-set cases, and the 2014 block-path theorem (Combinatorica 2016) settles a further class while leaving the general Solidity Conjecture open.
problem_asks: Part 1 (existence side): for which finite sets C of graphs does there exist a countable C-free graph U such that every countable C-free graph embeds into U as an induced subgraph ('strong embedding', as the literature uses the term; the statement does not define it). Part 2 (nonexistence side): for the remaining finite sets C, show no such U exists; the question as stated asks for the full set of finite C on which the answer is yes, so both sides are needed for a characterisation. Parts of the wording the statement does not fix: (a) C-free is read in the literature as 'contains no subgraph (not necessarily induced) isomorphic to a member of C'; (b) the statement does not say whether members of C must be connected, or whether C may contain several graphs (the literature treats finite families, and reduces some cases to connected members); (c) the statement names only countable graphs, so uncountable universal graphs are not asked about; (d) it does not ask for a single universal graph homogeneous or of oligomorphic automorphism group, though those are open follow-up questions in Cherlin's talks.

events.what_happened: Komjáth and Pach, 'Universal graphs without large bipartite subgraphs', Mathematika 31 (1984) 282-290. Studies graphs on gamma vertices omitting a complete bipartite K_{alpha,beta}; the abstract excerpt I could read gives an if-and-only-if: a universal element exists iff (i) gamma > omega or (ii) gamma = omega, alpha = 1 and beta <= 3. Secondary sources (Cherlin's survey slides as quoted in a search summary, and Siniora 2017) list countable K_{m,n}-free classes as having no universal member, attributing this to Komjáth and Pach 1984. I did not read the full paper.
events.delivers: Per the excerpt: a classification of universality for K_{alpha,beta}-free graphs on gamma vertices, for the cases read off the abstract. Per secondary sources: no countable universal K_{m,n}-free graph for finite m,n with m >= 2 (not confirmed against the paper). Restriction: complete bipartite forbidden graphs only, not general finite C.
events.remains: Every finite C that is not a complete bipartite graph; and the countable K_{m,n} claim is unconfirmed from the primary text.

checked_by.who: Mathematika (refereed journal of record, Cambridge/London Math Society)

events.doubts: I read only the abstract excerpt from the Cambridge page, and the class symbols in its final lines are images. The countable K_{m,n} nonexistence is attributed to this paper only by secondary sources. Kojman 1995 and Shelah 2012 treat the uncountable and GCH cases of the same family, so the countable finite-(m,n) reading should be checked against the paper itself.
events.direction: Negative for the bipartite cases covered (per secondary sources), and a positive classification for K_{1,beta} with beta <= 3 per the abstract excerpt. The question asks for finite C generally, so the answer to the bullet from this event is partial and for complete bipartite C only.

events.what_happened: Komjáth, Mekler and Pach, 'Some universal graphs', Israel J. Math. 64 (1988) 158-168. Per secondary summaries (Cherlin-Shi cycles paper; Krill 2023 introduction): for every odd k >= 3 there is a universal countable graph for the class of graphs omitting all odd cycles of length at most k (as subgraph embeddings in the summary; strong/weak not confirmed). The abstract also states that the classes omitting all paths of length n and omitting all circuits of length at least n have universal elements in all infinite powers.
events.delivers: Existence for finite sets of odd cycles {C3, C5, ..., C_(2k+1)} (per summary), existence for the single path P_n (omitting paths of length n), and existence for the infinite family of cycles of length at least n. Restriction: these families; odd-cycle sets are the only finite sets of cycles that admit a universal member, by the converse in the Cherlin-Shi event below.
events.remains: Finite sets of C that mix cycles with non-cycles, or that are not of the listed shapes; and the strong-vs-weak status of the existence claims, which the search summaries did not settle.

checked_by.who: Israel Journal of Mathematics (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, vol. 64, pp. 158-168

events.doubts: The full text was not read; the statements come from Cherlin-Shi's and Krill's summaries and from a search snippet of the abstract. Krill's 2023 paper calls the cycle case 'proved by Komjáth, Mekler and Pach' with a strong (induced) universal graph in the minor setting, which may or may not match the subgraph version.
events.direction: Positive (existence) for the cycle, path and long-cycle families named above.
events.object: Existence only, from the summaries: a countable graph containing every countable graph with no odd cycle of length at most k as a subgraph (per summary). No explicit construction recorded in the sources I read; existence is non-constructive as far as I could tell.

events.what_happened: Cherlin and Komjáth, 'There is no universal countable pentagon-free graph' (Rutgers copy labelled 1993). Per the search summary, for any circuit G of length at least 4 there is no universal countable G-free graph; this covers C5 and, per Cherlin-Komjáth's attribution, C4 was earlier shown by J. Pach. The PDF itself was not readable.
events.revisions: Rutgers copy labelled 1993; the journal publication was not confirmed in the sources I found.
events.delivers: Nonexistence of a universal countable C_n-free graph for each single cycle C_n with n >= 4 (per summary). Restriction: single cycles only.
events.remains: Single non-cycle C; finite sets of cycles (see the Cherlin-Shi and Komjáth-Mekler-Pach events); and the strong/weak sense is not confirmed.
events.doubts: Publication status not confirmed. The strong/weak sense of nonexistence is not stated in the summary I read, but nonexistence for weak (subgraph) universality implies nonexistence for strong (induced) universality, since an induced embedding is a subgraph embedding, so the nonexistence claim transfers to the bullet's sense if the result is in the weak sense.
events.direction: Negative: for each single cycle of length >= 4 the answer to the bullet's question is no.

events.what_happened: Cherlin and Shi, 'Graphs omitting a finite set of cycles' (Rutgers copy labelled 1994; a version marked 'Revised, 2022' was also found). Per the search summary: if a finite set C of cycles admits a universal C-free graph, then C consists precisely of all odd cycles of order less than some bound, i.e. {C3, C5, ..., C_(2k+1)}. The converse was proved by Komjáth, Mekler and Pach (1988). The paper also asks for an effective criterion for a finite set of forbidden subgraphs to be a Rado constraint, noting joint embedding is necessary.
events.revisions: Rutgers copy labelled 1994; revised version dated 2022 (per search snippet).
events.delivers: Complete characterisation for finite sets consisting entirely of cycles: universal member exists iff the set is the odd-cycle initial segment (with the converse from KMP 1988). Restriction: sets of cycles only.
events.remains: Finite sets mixing cycles with other graphs; the effective-criterion question for general finite sets (asked, not answered in the summary).
events.doubts: Read only as a search snippet and summary of the Rutgers PDF, which was not readable as text. Journal publication not confirmed. The 2022 revision is a working draft per its header ('with additional remarks; not checked'), per the summary I read.
events.direction: Negative for every finite cycle set other than odd-cycle initial segments; positive for the odd-cycle initial segments (via KMP).

events.what_happened: Goldstern and Kojman, 'Universal bridge-free graphs', arXiv math/9409206 (submitted 6 Sep 1994). Defines an infinite family of finite trees B_n ('bridges') and shows no countable universal B_n-free graph exists for any n; also shows no countable universal graph among graphs omitting all cycles of length at most 2k for k >= 2 (using an idea of S. Mozes). Poses the open question whether a countable universal graph exists among graphs omitting all cycles.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 (6 Sep 1994); no later version found.
events.delivers: Nonexistence for each single bridge B_n (a tree) and for the finite family of all cycles of length at most 2k (k >= 2). Restriction: these specific trees and cycle families; the finite-set-of-cycles case with odd lengths is treated by KMP and Cherlin-Shi.
events.remains: Other finite trees; the infinite family of all cycles (open as a question in the paper, per summary); general finite C.
events.doubts: Journal publication not confirmed (a DOI 10.1007/BF00052907 appeared in one search result, not opened). Read from arXiv abstract and a summary; the arXiv PDF was not fetched as text.
events.direction: Negative for the listed bridges and the even-cycle-bounded families; the question of all cycles is open as posed in the paper.

events.what_happened: Füredi and Komjáth, 'On the existence of countable universal graphs', J. Graph Theory (1997), per a search summary; a companion Combinatorica (1997) paper handles trees: a finite tree with a vertex of degree at least 4 adjacent to a leaf (with unique largest-degree vertex, per summary) has no countable universal G-free graph. Main negative theorem as summarised: for finite, 2-connected, non-complete G, the class of countable G-free graphs has no universal element.
events.delivers: Nonexistence for every single finite 2-connected non-complete graph G (in the subgraph-universal sense per summary, which implies the induced sense). Also nonexistence for a class of trees per the Combinatorica companion.
events.remains: Single C that are not 2-connected (including connected C with cut vertices and non-complete blocks other than the block-path case), and all finite sets of C.

checked_by.who: Journal of Graph Theory and Combinatorica (refereed journals of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the two papers

events.doubts: Full text not read (PDF on Füredi's site was not opened). The statement is taken from the abstract and secondary citations, including the Cherlin-Shelah 2014 paper that calls it a 'Füredi-Komjáth hypergraph construction'. The sense of universality (weak or strong) should be checked against the paper.
events.direction: Negative for all single 2-connected non-complete C.

events.what_happened: Cherlin, Shelah and Shi, 'Universal graphs with forbidden subgraphs and algebraic closure', arXiv math/9809202 (submitted 15 Sep 1998), Adv. in Appl. Math. 22 (1999) 454-491. Model-theoretic framework: for finitely many forbidden connected subgraphs the existence question largely reduces to local finiteness of an associated algebraic closure operator acl; the paper gives a criterion for the existence of a universal C-free graph via existential completeness and acl, and gives new examples plus simpler proofs of known cases. Per a later Cherlin talk: for finite sets C of connected graphs, the model companion of C-free graphs is aleph_0-categorical iff acl_C is locally finite.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 (15 Sep 1998); journal Adv. Appl. Math. 22 (1999).
events.delivers: A criterion (local finiteness of acl) that reduces existence for finite sets of connected forbidden graphs to a property of acl; the abstract does not say which specific C are settled. Per summaries it gives new examples of universal C-free graphs, e.g. the bowtie (see Siniora 2017 event).
events.remains: The local-finiteness property itself must be checked for each finite C; the paper does not give a closed classification.

checked_by.who: Advances in Applied Mathematics (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, vol. 22, pp. 454-491

events.doubts: I read the abstract (condensed) only; the PDF was not read as text. The 'algebraic closure' criterion is described by the abstract as largely reducing the question, which is not a settlement.
events.direction: Reduction rather than a verdict: relates existence for each finite connected C to local finiteness of acl. Positive examples are given but not listed in the abstract.

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'Universality among graphs omitting a complete bipartite graph', arXiv math/0102058 (v1 7 Feb 2001; v2 17 May 2010), Sh:706, Combinatorica 32 no. 3 (2012) 325-362. Per the abstract: for cardinals lambda, kappa, theta, considers graphs of cardinality lambda with no subgraph that is a (kappa, theta)-complete bipartite graph; asks whether a universal one exists under (weak) embedding; 'We solve this problem completely under GCH'; under various cardinal-arithmetic assumptions proves nonexistence.
events.revisions: v1 7 Feb 2001; v2 17 May 2010; journal Combinatorica 32 (2012).
events.delivers: Universality among graphs omitting a complete bipartite graph K_{kappa,theta}, for all cardinals under GCH; nonexistence under various cardinal-arithmetic hypotheses. Whether the countable case of finite K_{m,n} is covered was not confirmed from the abstract (the abstract is stated for arbitrary cardinals and may include aleph_0).
events.remains: Non-bipartite forbidden graphs; finite sets of C; and the countable finite-(m,n) reading is unconfirmed.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal publication, vol. 32 no. 3 (2012), pp. 325-362

events.doubts: I read the arXiv abstract and metadata only (the PDF was not opened as text). The abstract refers to 'weak embedding'; whether strong embeddings are also covered is not stated.
events.direction: For the bipartite case, a full answer under GCH (existence/nonexistence depending on cardinals); per the Cherlin-Shelah context, nonexistence in the countable finite-(m,n) case is attributed elsewhere. Direction for the bullet's countable finite-C question is not established by this abstract.

events.what_happened: Higasikawa, 'There is no universal countable random-free graph', arXiv math/0106102 (submitted 13 Jun 2001), 3 pages. Shows that the class of countable graphs into which the random graph does not embed has no universal member under strong (induced) embeddings. Notes that a result of Diestel, Halin and Volger about weak embeddability is often misquoted for the strong setting.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 (13 Jun 2001); no later version found.
events.delivers: Nonexistence for the class of countable graphs omitting the random graph R (an infinite forbidden graph, by embedding). This is a different constraint: it forbids an infinite graph as an embedded copy, not finitely many finite graphs as subgraphs.
events.remains: The bullet's finite-C question is untouched; this event is recorded as a discounted near-neighbour.
events.doubts: Scope: the forbidden object is the infinite random graph, not a finite C. Read from the abstract and introduction via search; the full proof was not read.
events.direction: Negative, but for a different class (graphs not containing the random graph), so it does not answer the bullet's question.

events.what_happened: Cherlin and Shelah, 'Universal graphs with a forbidden subtree', arXiv math/0512218 (submitted 10 Dec 2005; one version), J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 97 (2007) 293-333. Characterises the finite trees T for which a universal countable T-free graph exists, by a new inductive method and a pruning technique that reduces forbidden graphs (viewed as trees of blocks) to critical cases. Confirms Tallgren's conjecture for trees. Per a 2011-era summary, the Cherlin-Shi-Tallgren form of the criterion: for a tree T of order n, a universal countable T-free graph exists iff T contains a path of order n-1 (i.e. T is a path or a path plus one pendant edge).
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only (10 Dec 2005); journal JCTB 97 (2007).
events.delivers: A complete answer for each single finite tree T: universal countable T-free graph exists iff T is a path or obtained from a path by attaching one extra edge (per summary). The abstract does not state strong or weak universality; the summary's criterion is the one I could read.
events.remains: Single connected C that are not trees; finite sets of trees (not stated as covered by the abstract).

checked_by.who: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal publication, vol. 97 no. 3 (2007) pp. 293-333

events.doubts: The tree criterion is taken from a search summary (Cherlin-Shi-Tallgren form) rather than from the paper's theorem, which I could not read. Strong vs weak sense not confirmed.
events.direction: Positive for trees that are paths or path-plus-one-edge; negative for other trees (per summary).

events.what_happened: Cherlin and Tallgren, 'Universal graphs with a forbidden near-path or 2-bouquet' (Rutgers PDF dated 15 Apr 2013). Per its abstract as read in a search snippet: for a tree arising from a path by adding one extra edge, a universal countable C-free graph exists; and the 2-bouquets C (two complete graphs sharing exactly one vertex) that admit a universal countable C-free graph are determined. A 2-bouquet criterion (min(m,n) <= 5 and (m,n) != (5,5)) appears in a search summary for B_{m,n} = K_m and K_n glued at a vertex; that criterion is not confirmed against the paper. Journal reference 'JGT 56 (2007) 41-63' appeared in a search summary and was not confirmed.
events.revisions: Rutgers PDF dated 15 Apr 2013 (version); earliest arXiv or first-written date not found.
events.delivers: Existence for path-plus-one-edge trees; a classification of universal existence for 2-bouquets (per the abstract as read; the exact criterion not confirmed). Restriction: these families.
events.remains: Finite C of other shapes, and sets of C.
events.doubts: The date 2007 comes from an unconfirmed journal citation in a summary; the Rutgers copy is dated 2013. The 2-bouquet criterion was read from a summary, not the paper. Treat the date and the criterion as provisional.
events.direction: Positive for path-plus-one-edge trees and for the 2-bouquets in the determined range; negative for the rest (per summary).

events.what_happened: Krill, 'Universal graphs with forbidden wheel minors', arXiv 2309.12473 (submitted 21 Sep 2023). For a wheel W, the class of countable graphs with no W minor contains a graph that has every graph in the class as an induced subgraph (strong universality). Notes that for non-planar X there cannot be a weakly universal X-minor-free graph.
events.revisions: One version (v1 21 Sep 2023) per the arXiv page.
events.delivers: Strong universality for the class of countable graphs excluding a single wheel as a minor. Restriction: minor exclusion, not subgraph exclusion.
events.remains: The bullet's subgraph-free classes for finite C. Discounted as a different question (minors, not subgraphs).
events.doubts: Scope: minor-excluded classes. Not a subgraph-free class, so it does not settle the bullet's question for any finite C. Journal publication not found.
events.direction: Positive (strong universality) for minor-excluded classes; it cuts in a different direction setting: it is not about the bullet's classes.

events.what_happened: Panagiotopoulos and Tent, 'Universality vs Genericity and C4-free graphs', arXiv 2104.13222 (v1 27 Apr 2021; v2 22 Jun 2022, current). Shows that for an approximable class of countable structures, existence of a universal structure implies existence of a generic structure (converse fails). Proves that the class of all countable C4-free graphs has no generic structure, strengthening a result of Hajnal and Pach (who showed there is no universal countable C4-free graph; attribution varies per a secondary source, which credits J. Pach).
events.revisions: v1 27 Apr 2021; v2 22 Jun 2022 (current). Journal reference not on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: Nonexistence of a generic countable C4-free graph; combined with universal implies generic for approximable classes (from the abstract), this gives nonexistence of a universal countable C4-free graph in the strong sense if the class is approximable, which the abstract does not state directly.
events.remains: Other finite C; finite sets C. The inference that the result implies no universal member is mine, from the abstract's framing, and is not stated by the authors in the abstract.
events.doubts: Whether the class of countable C4-free graphs is approximable is not in the abstract I read. The C4 universality nonexistence is attributed to Hajnal-Pach and to J. Pach; the attribution differs across sources. A ScienceDirect version of the paper (S0195669822000865) returned HTTP 403 and was not read; the arXiv version was used.
events.direction: Negative for C = C4 (the strong-embedding universality question for the class of all countable C4-free graphs), via genericity. The inference is mine.

events.what_happened: Cherlin and Shelah, 'Universal graphs with a forbidden subgraph: Block path solidity', arXiv 1404.5757 (submitted 23 Apr 2014; one arXiv version), Combinatorica 36 no. 3 (2016) 249-264. Main theorem: let C be a finite connected graph whose tree of blocks is a path; if there is a (weakly) universal C-free graph, then the blocks of C are complete; generalises a result of Füredi and Komjáth. Shows the Pathlike Conjecture implies the Solidity Conjecture, and states the Solidity Conjecture for arbitrary finite connected C with a countable universal C-free graph: the blocks of C are complete. Also states open problems: determine when a universal C-free graph exists; whether an algorithm decides this for finite sets of connected graphs.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 (23 Apr 2014) only per the arXiv page. Cherlin's Rutgers site hosts a longer draft 'Universal graphs with a forbidden block path' (BlockPathv2, dated Aug 2014), which I could not read as text.
events.delivers: Nonexistence for connected C with path block tree and at least one non-complete block (the contrapositive of the main theorem); the Solidity Conjecture for those C. Restriction: block-path C only; general C with a non-path block tree is not settled.
events.remains: Connected C whose block tree is not a path (including C with one non-complete block that is not 2-connected, and the general Solidity and Pathlike conjectures); all disconnected C and finite sets of C; and the decidability question.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal publication, vol. 36 no. 3 (2016) pp. 249-264

events.doubts: Read from the arXiv abstract (via arXiv and ar5iv) and search summaries; the arXiv PDF was not readable as text, so the Solidity and Pathlike conjectures are quoted from the ar5iv summary and search snippets. The solidity conjecture is still listed as open in Cherlin's 2013 talk ('Ongoing'). No erratum or comment was found in searches, but citation-database checks (Google Scholar, MathSciNet) were not available.
events.direction: Negative for connected block-path C (non-complete block forces no universal member); positive for complete-block C in the same class is not established by the theorem as stated.

events.what_happened: Siniora, 'Bowtie-free graphs and generic automorphisms', arXiv 1705.01347 (v1 3 May 2017; v2 5 Apr 2023). Abstract: 'We show that the countable universal omega-categorical bowtie-free graph admits generic automorphisms. Moreover, we show that this graph is not finitely homogenisable.' So the abstract presupposes existence of a countable universal bowtie-free graph (C = bowtie, a single connected graph of order 5), attributed in the text to Komjáth and to the Cherlin-Shelah-Shi framework.
events.revisions: v1 3 May 2017; v2 5 Apr 2023 (both before the window).
events.delivers: Existence of an omega-categorical universal bowtie-free graph (per the abstract's presupposition) and its automorphism-group properties. Settles existence for the single bowtie (sense of universality not stated in the abstract; the omega-categorical construction is a model-theoretic one, which in summaries is taken to be a strong universal object).
events.remains: Other C. The paper does not address finite sets of C.
events.doubts: I read only the abstract and summary. The strong/weak sense of the bowtie universal graph is not confirmed by the abstract; the claim that it is strong is from a search summary. Journal publication not found.
events.direction: Positive for C = bowtie (the existence side of the bullet's question for this single C).
events.object: Existence of the countable universal omega-categorical bowtie-free graph (the object itself is not described in the abstract). The paper studies its automorphisms: generic automorphisms exist, and the graph is not finitely homogenisable.

events.what_happened: Cherlin and Shi, 'Graphs Omitting Sums of Complete Graphs', Rutgers PDF (file labelled 2022; header 'with additional remarks; not checked'). Per the search summary: for every finite m and n, there is a finite set {G1,...,Gl} of countable (m.K_n)-free graphs such that every countable (m.K_n)-free graph embeds as an induced subgraph in at least one Gi. This is a finite family of targets, not a single universal member. Also gives size estimates for special cases.
events.revisions: Rutgers draft (labelled 2022), not confirmed as published.
events.delivers: A finite universal family for each finite sum m.K_n of complete graphs. Different question from a single universal member; not a settlement of the bullet for any finite C.
events.remains: Whether a single universal member exists for those C (not claimed).
events.doubts: Read from a search summary of a Rutgers PDF that was not readable as text; the 2022 date is from the filename. The header says the draft is 'not checked'.
events.direction: Does not answer the bullet's question for any C: finite universal families, not single universal members.

events.what_happened: Bastide, Esperet, Groenland, Hilaire, Rambaud and Wesolek, 'Faithful universal graphs for minor-closed classes', arXiv 2504.19582 (v1 28 Apr 2025; v2 16 May 2025; v3 23 Aug 2025; v4 4 May 2026). Builds on Huynh-Mohar-Samal-Thomassen-Wood (2021). Finite quantitative result: a K_t-minor-free graph containing every n-vertex planar graph as a subgraph must have 2^Omega(n) vertices; polynomial-size K_4- and K_7-minor-free universal graphs for trees and K_4-minor-free graphs (induced); universal graphs for bounded degree/treedepth/pathwidth/treewidth classes.
events.revisions: v1 28 Apr 2025; v2 16 May 2025; v3 23 Aug 2025; v4 4 May 2026 (current).
events.delivers: Quantitative universality results for minor-closed (K_t-minor-free) classes at finite n. Scope: forbidden minors, finite graphs; not countable universal members for C-free classes.
events.remains: The bullet's countable subgraph-free question for finite C is untouched. Discounted as a different question.
events.time_since_posted: about 17 months since v1; about 5 months since v4
events.doubts: A search summary said the paper's reference list includes the Cherlin-Shelah papers, but the arXiv page I fetched did not mention Cherlin-Shelah; the conflict is unresolved (I did not open the full text). Whether this paper is in any way a neighbour of the bullet depends on whether the judging pass considers minor-closed classes related to C-free classes; I record it as discounted.
events.direction: Does not bear on the bullet for any finite C; it concerns minor-excluded classes at finite n.

events.what_happened: Aurichi and Pinto, 'Universal Families of Rayless Graphs', arXiv 2512.15612 (v1 submitted 17 Dec 2025; math.CO). Studies strong complexity (the least size of a strongly universal family) for rayless graphs of size at most kappa. Shows that for each infinite kappa the rayless graphs of size at most kappa admit a strongly universal family of size kappa+, and no smaller family works. Section 4 ('Forbidding finite subgraphs') Theorem 4.4: for a finite family K of finite graphs, the class of K-free rayless graphs has strong complexity kappa+ (= aleph_1 for kappa = aleph_0) unless some member of K is a subdivision of a star, in which case the complexity is at most aleph_0. Question 4.10 (open): whether for some finite K the countable complexity exceeds aleph_1 is consistent with ZFC.
events.revisions: v1 17 Dec 2025 only (per the arXiv page I opened); no later version found.
events.delivers: For countable K-free rayless graphs with K a finite set of finite graphs (not containing a star subdivision): no countable strongly universal family exists (complexity aleph_1), so in particular no single strongly universal member. Restriction: the host class is rayless graphs (no infinite ray), the object is a universal family rather than a single member, and the result is about K-free rayless graphs, not all countable K-free graphs.
events.remains: The bullet's question for all countable C-free graphs (not rayless) and for single universal members; for star-subdivision-containing K, the countable complexity bound is at most aleph_0 (a countable family exists), which again is not a single member.
events.doubts: Scope: rayless is a restriction of the bullet's class, so the result is about a different class and a different object. The authors' Section 2 and Definition 2.6 disagree on whether the class is connected rayless graphs or kappa-rayless graphs, which the judging pass should note. A search snippet described the paper as citing Cherlin-related work on forbidden subgraphs, but I did not confirm whether it cites Cherlin-Shelah's single-member results. No public engagement found in my searches.
events.direction: Negative for the rayless, finite-K, countable-complexity question (no countable strongly universal family when K contains no star subdivision); does not cut the bullet's question either way.

disputes.summary: Attribution of the nonexistence of a universal countable C4-free graph differs across sources: one survey credits Hajnal and Pach; Cherlin and Komjáth credit J. Pach. The Panagiotopoulos-Tent abstract cites a result of Hajnal and Pach. Not resolved here.

Attribution of the bowtie-free universal graph: a search summary credits Komjáth with the existence proof, and says Komjáth's construction was not reachable by Fraïssé amalgamation; Cherlin-Shelah-Shi (1999) gave the model-theoretic route. Siniora (2017) presupposes the same object. Not resolved here.

summary: The bullet asks for the characterisation of all finite sets C of graphs for which a countable C-free graph exists into which every countable C-free graph embeds as an induced subgraph. I found 48 web searches' worth of material and opened around 25 sources (arXiv abstracts and HTML, the Wikipedia list, the Cambridge page for the Komjáth-Pach paper, Cherlin's Rutgers publication index, and ar5iv for the 2014 paper). Many Rutgers PDFs, the Cherlin 2014 full text, the 2019 CUNY slides and the ScienceDirect C4 paper were not readable, so the open-problem statuses rest on abstracts, search summaries and snippets. Within the window, nothing I found settles or moves the general question. The two in-window papers are about other classes: Aurichi and Pinto (arXiv 2512.15612, 17 Dec 2025) on rayless graphs with universal families, where for countable K-free rayless graphs the strong complexity is aleph_1 unless K contains a star subdivision; and Bastide et al. (arXiv 2504.19582, first posted 28 Apr 2025) on minor-closed classes. Before the window, the literature decides several families: nonexistence for every single 2-connected non-complete C (Füredi-Komjáth 1997); for finite cycle sets, exactly the odd-cycle initial segments admit a universal member (Cherlin-Shi with Komjáth-Mekler-Pach 1988); nonexistence for single cycles of length at least 4 (Cherlin-Komjáth 1993) and bridges (Goldstern-Kojman 1994); the tree case in full (Cherlin-Shelah 2005/2007); the bowtie (existence, Siniora 2017 presupposing Komjáth and Cherlin-Shelah-Shi); and the block-path case of connected C, which by Cherlin-Shelah 2014 (Combinatorica 2016) has complete blocks whenever a universal member exists. The general Solidity Conjecture and Pathlike Conjecture are stated as open in that paper and listed as 'Ongoing' in Cherlin's 2013 talk; I found no proof of either in any source, including Cherlin's cached publication index, which lists no universality paper after 2016. Close calls for the judging pass: (a) Does the block-path theorem count as settling a restricted class of the bullet? It settles one-sided cases for connected C with path block trees, and the bullet asks about all finite sets, including disconnected C and families; (b) Does the Aurichi-Pinto complexity result count as a case of this bullet? Its host class is rayless, and its object is a universal family, so as stated it does not, but it is the closest in-window item and the countable K-free complexity claim has the same shape; (c) Does the Wikipedia 'strong embeddings' wording match the literature's induced-subgraph meaning? I assumed yes. Note the asymmetry the judging pass should use: strong (induced) existence implies weak existence, and weak nonexistence implies strong nonexistence. Wikipedia citation: the bullet appears under 'Model theory and formal languages' with citation [160] in the cached current page; an older mirror shows the same bullet with citation [103], which is Cherlin-Shelah, 'Universal graphs with a forbidden subtree', JCTB 2007. The text of [160] in the 26 January 2024 revision was not retrieved. AI involvement: none found. Searches for AI results on this problem, including the AI counterexample preprint 'GPT, the Counterexample Machine' (Sra, 30 Aug 2026), the AIMath and 'Vibe Mathed' trackers (secondary counts only; AIMath site not reached), the Google DeepMind Formal Conjectures repository (GitHub code search requires sign-in), Gil Kalai's blog (not reached) and OpenAI's 'ten advances' page (HTTP 403), returned nothing tying an AI system to this problem. The AI results that did surface (Erdős unit distance, Hadwiger and Sidorenko announcements, Erdős degeneracy disproof, Dinitz-Garg-Goemans) are on other problems. Those AI-tracker checks are not exhaustive, so 'none_found' is a finding from my searches, not a complete audit.
competing_reading: The strongest case for reading the record as more settled: the bullet's content can be read as covering the single-C and cycle-set cases, and on that reading the literature decides most of them. Füredi-Komjáth 1997 handles every single 2-connected non-complete C; the tree case is complete (Cherlin-Shelah 2007); the cycle-set case is complete (Cherlin-Shi plus KMP 1988); and the block-path case is complete for connected C (2014). Under that reading, what remains is the mixed-block, non-tree, connected C case plus all finite sets that mix shapes; that is a large but narrower open area than 'the whole question'. The reverse reading, against that: the bullet asks for finite sets C, not single graphs, and the literature covers many fewer finite sets than single graphs; in particular the statement's wording about disconnected members and families is not handled by any single paper I found.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Full text of Cherlin-Shelah, Combinatorica 36 (2016), to read the exact Solidity and Pathlike conjectures and any status note, and to confirm whether 'universal' there means strong or weak. (2) The text of Wikipedia's citation [160] in the 26 January 2024 revision, to confirm which source the bullet cites. (3) Cherlin's 2014 BlockPathv2 draft and the 2019 CUNY slide list of open problems, read as text, for their status as of their dates. (4) A citing-papers check (Google Scholar, MathSciNet, zbMATH) for arXiv 1404.5757 and math/0512218 covering 2024-2026, to test whether any in-window paper resolves the Solidity or Pathlike conjectures. (5) Full reads of Komjáth-Pach 1984 and Shelah Sh:706 for the countable finite K_{m,n} case, and of Füredi-Komjáth 1997 for the strong-vs-weak sense. (6) The Formal Conjectures Lean file for this problem, if one exists, which may show how the repository formalises the statement.
